title: Cartesian small etale restriction of big-fppf module sheaves
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $p:\mathcal X\to\mathit{Sch}/S$ be a category fibred in groupoids [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], with its big fppf topology and regular-function structure sheaf $\mathcal O_{\mathcal X}$ from [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra]. For $x\in\mathcal X(T)$, the projection functor $\mathcal X/x\to\mathit{Sch}/T$ sends an arrow to its underlying scheme arrow. It is an equivalence: cartesian lifting supplies essential surjectivity and cartesian uniqueness supplies bijections on arrows. Compose the forgetful functor $T_{\mathrm{et}}\to\mathit{Sch}/T$ for the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] with an inverse of this equivalence to obtain $\lambda_x:T_{\mathrm{et}}\to\mathcal X/x$, and with $\mathcal X/x\to\mathcal X$ to obtain $\widetilde\lambda_x$. The counit identifies the scheme below $\widetilde\lambda_x(V\to T)$ with $V$. The lift is continuous for the small etale and big fppf topologies: an etale covering lifts to an fppf covering and cartesian uniqueness identifies its matching diagrams. Define $\mathcal O_{x,\mathrm{et}}=\widetilde\lambda_x^*\mathcal O_{\mathcal X}$ by precomposition; thus on a lifted etale test it is the original regular-function ring, canonically $\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$, in the total site's common coefficient universe. For module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] define $\mathrm{res}_{x,\mathrm{et}}:\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_{\mathcal X})\to\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_{x,\mathrm{et}})$ by the same precomposition on sections and linear maps, equivalently the continuous module pushforward along $\widetilde\lambda_x$ with the identity ring map. For every arrow $a:y\to x$ above $u:T'\to T$ and every etale test $V\to T$, let its lifted restriction arrow be the unique arrow $\widetilde\lambda_y(T'\times_T V)\to\widetilde\lambda_x(V)$ lying above the fibre-product projection under the counit identifications, and whose composite to $x$ equals the composite through $y$ and $a$. The required base triangle follows from the counits and the fibre-product equation. These arrows are natural in $V$, by faithfulness of the slice comparison, and define the corresponding restriction natural transformation. No algebraicity, quasi-coherence, flatness, or finiteness hypothesis is needed for these constructions.

source.place: section-locally-quasi-coherent; equation-comparison-modules preceding definition-flat-base-change; definition-pullback: restriction to a test scheme by cartesian lifts.

proof.text: Put $P_x:\mathcal X/x\to\mathit{Sch}/T$. Apply [lem-sfb-fibred-test-object-ringed-localization] with $\mathcal C=\mathcal X$, $U=T$ and $\tau=\mathrm{fppf}$. Its hypotheses are exactly the fibred-groupoid and inherited fppf-site hypotheses here. It gives the equivalence $P_x$ and the regular-function identification. Choose a quasi-inverse $Q_x$ with counit $\epsilon:P_xQ_x\simeq\mathrm{id}$. Let $i:T_{\mathrm{et}}\to\mathit{Sch}/T$ be the forgetful functor of [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]; define $\lambda_x=Q_xi$ and $L_x=\widetilde\lambda_x$ by forgetting the arrow to $x$. Write $q_V:L_x(V)\to x$ and $\epsilon_V:p(L_x(V))\simeq V$. The counit is a morphism over $T$, so $p(q_V)=v\epsilon_V$ for $v:V\to T$. These are the required scheme identifications; the choice is a quasi-inverse to an equivalence, not a choice of unrelated data.

For a covering $\{V_i\to V\}$ in $T_{\mathrm{et}}$, the underlying maps of $\{L_x(V_i)\to L_x(V)\}$ are identified with $\{V_i\to V\}$ by naturality of $\epsilon$. Each is flat and locally of finite presentation by [def-weil-etale-morphism], and they are jointly surjective. Hence the lifted family is fppf by [def-pc-fppf-site], and covers the total site by [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra]. For any $W\to V$ in $T_{\mathrm{et}}$, its pullback with $V_i\to V$ is the scheme pullback by [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Every total-category arrow is strongly cartesian by the unique-factorization clause of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Apply [lem-sfb-cartesian-lift-pullback-square] to $L_x(V_i)\to L_x(V)\leftarrow L_x(W)$: its base pullback is the scheme $V_i\times_VW$ after the counit identifications, and the arrow from $L_x(V_i\times_VW)$ to $L_x(W)$ is a cartesian lift of its projection. Thus the canonical comparison to the total-category pullback is an isomorphism. This verifies both conditions of continuity in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](3), including preservation of the overlaps.

By [lem-weil-pbc-site-continuous-pushforward-sheaf], precomposition with $L_x$ sends sheaves of sets and abelian groups to sheaves. Set $\mathcal O_{x,\mathrm{et}}(V)=\mathcal O_{\mathcal X}(L_x(V))$ and $(\mathrm{res}_{x,\mathrm{et}}M)(V)=M(L_x(V))$. Retain the original ring operations, module actions and restrictions. The module semilinearity equation of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] is unchanged under precomposition; ring and module axioms hold at every object. On a module morphism $f$, use the linear component $f_{L_x(V)}$; identities and composition are inherited componentwise. Thus this defines the claimed functor on module sheaves. The ring identification in [lem-sfb-fibred-test-object-ringed-localization] identifies these coefficient rings canonically with $\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$, with the same restriction maps. With the coefficient ring defined as this precomposition, its structure map to itself is the identity, so the construction is precisely continuous module pushforward with that ring map. All evaluations use the common universe fixed in the hypothesis.

Fix $a:y\to x$ over $u:T'\to T$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits], $B_u(V)=T'\times_TV$ is a functor on small etale tests, with projections $r_V:B_u(V)\to V$ and $b_V:B_u(V)\to T'$. Write $\epsilon^x_V:p(L_x(V))\simeq V$ and $\epsilon^y_{B_u(V)}:p(L_y(B_u(V)))\simeq B_u(V)$. The required underlying arrow is $h_V=(\epsilon^x_V)^{-1}r_V\epsilon^y_{B_u(V)}$. The counit identities from step 1 and the fibre-product equation $v r_V=u b_V$ of [def-pc-fibre-product] give
$$p(q^x_V)h_V=v\epsilon^x_V(\epsilon^x_V)^{-1}r_V\epsilon^y_{B_u(V)}=u b_V\epsilon^y_{B_u(V)}=p(aq^y_{B_u(V)}).$$
Thus $h_V$ is a morphism in the scheme slice from $P_x(aq^y_{B_u(V)})$ to $P_x(q^x_V)$. The equivalence in [lem-sfb-fibred-test-object-ringed-localization] gives a unique preimage $t_V:L_y(B_u(V))\to L_x(V)$ in the slice over $x$. In particular $q^x_Vt_V=aq^y_{B_u(V)}$ and $p(t_V)=h_V$. This proves existence and uniqueness with the precise base triangle.

Let $f:V\to W$ be a morphism of etale tests. Both $L_x(f)t_V$ and $t_WL_y(B_u(f))$ are arrows from $(L_y(B_u(V)),aq^y_{B_u(V)})$ to $(L_x(W),q^x_W)$ in $\mathcal X/x$: the triangles follow from the definition of $Q_xi$ and $Q_yi$ as functors into the slices, and from step 4. Naturality of the counits gives
$$p(L_x(f))h_V=(\epsilon^x_W)^{-1}f r_V\epsilon^y_{B_u(V)},\qquad h_Wp(L_y(B_u(f)))=(\epsilon^x_W)^{-1}r_W B_u(f)\epsilon^y_{B_u(V)}.$$
These are equal because $f r_V=r_WB_u(f)$, the defining projection equation for the induced fibre-product map in [def-pc-fibre-product]. Faithfulness of $P_x$ from [lem-sfb-fibred-test-object-ringed-localization] gives $L_x(f)t_V=t_WL_y(B_u(f))$. This is the naturality of $t:L_yB_u\to L_x$. Applying a module presheaf contravariantly gives its restriction comparison, natural also in module morphisms by their defining naturality square. No algebraicity, quasi-coherence, flatness of $u$, or finiteness was used.

def moduliEtaleRestriction {S : Scheme.{u}}
    (F : BasedCategory.{v, w} (Over S)) (hF : IsFibredInGroupoids F) (x : F.obj) :
    ringedSiteModules.{max (u + 1) v w} (moduliModuleRings F hF) ⥤
      ringedSiteModules.{max (u + 1) v w} (moduliEtaleModuleRings F hF x)
